directAnswer: Pope Clement VIII was Ippolito Aldobrandini, who reigned from 1592 to 1605. He reconciled King Henry IV of France to the Church in 1595, issued the corrected Sixto-Clementine Vulgate, annexed Ferrara to the Papal States, celebrated the Jubilee of 1600, and convened the Congregatio de Auxiliis on the debate over grace and free will.

sections.h2: Ippolito Aldobrandini, Lawyer and Legate to Poland
paras: Ippolito Aldobrandini was born at Fano on 24 February 1536, into a Florentine family exiled by the Medici. He trained in law and held offices in the Roman tribunals before Sixtus V made him a cardinal in 1585.

As papal legate to Poland in 1588 he negotiated the release of Archduke Maximilian of Austria, captured in a disputed royal election, which earned him the gratitude of the Habsburgs. Elected on 30 January 1592, he was known for intense personal piety and spent long hours in prayer and confession; the historian Caesar Baronius served as his confessor.

Clement VIII's most consequential decision concerned France. Henry of Navarre, the Protestant heir, had converted to Catholicism in 1593. Despite strong Spanish objections, Clement formally absolved him in September 1595, recognizing him as king.

The reconciliation helped end the French Wars of Religion and restored the balance between France and Spain in papal diplomacy. In 1598 Clement also secured the duchy of Ferrara for the Papal States after the Este line failed.

sections.h2: The Vulgate, the Liturgy, and the Union of Brest
paras: In 1592 Clement VIII issued the corrected Latin Bible known as the Sixto-Clementine Vulgate, which remained the official Latin text of the Catholic Church until the twentieth century. He also published revised editions of the Pontifical, the Breviary and the Missal, and a new Index of Forbidden Books in 1596.

In 1595 and 1596 bishops of the Ruthenian Church in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth entered communion with Rome while keeping their Byzantine liturgy, an agreement known as the Union of Brest. Clement created influential cardinals, among them Baronius and Robert Bellarmine.

sections.h2: Grace, the Ottomans, and the Jubilee of 1600
paras: In 1597 Clement VIII set up the Congregatio de Auxiliis to resolve a bitter dispute between Dominicans and Jesuits about how divine grace works with human freedom. The commission met for years without a final ruling, and Paul V later allowed both schools to continue teaching.

Clement supported the Habsburg war against the Ottoman Empire known as the Long War, sending troops and funds to Hungary. The Jubilee of 1600 drew enormous crowds to Rome. That same year the philosopher Giordano Bruno was burned in the Campo de' Fiori after a long trial by the Roman Inquisition, an event the Church has since acknowledged with regret. Clement VIII died on 3 March 1605.

keyFacts: Born Ippolito Aldobrandini at Fano on 24 February 1536
Absolved and recognized Henry IV of France (1595)
Annexed Ferrara to the Papal States (1598)
Union of Brest with the Ruthenian Church (1595 to 1596)

faqs.question: Why did Clement VIII absolve Henry IV?
faqs.answer: Henry had converted to Catholicism in 1593. Clement accepted his conversion in 1595 despite Spanish opposition, which helped bring peace to France after decades of religious war.

faqs.question: What was the Congregatio de Auxiliis?
faqs.answer: A papal commission begun in 1597 to settle a Dominican and Jesuit dispute about grace and free will. It ended under Paul V without a definitive decision, both views being permitted.

faqs.question: What is the Sixto-Clementine Vulgate?
faqs.answer: The corrected official Latin Bible published by Clement VIII in 1592, replacing the faulty edition of Sixtus V. It served as the Church's standard Latin text for centuries.
